newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-ROMANIA CLUBS, AUTHORITIES IN ROW OVER FEES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMANIA CLUBS, AUTHORITIES IN ROW OVER FEES.

text.p: Romania's top soccer clubs have asked the country's ruling national body to return money taken from them for the transfer of their players abroad.

"Over the last six years the Romanian Soccer Federation (FRF) has taken 10 percent from each player's transfer money," Steau Bucharest club president Marcel Puscas said. "This was against FIFA and UEFA rules which ban this kind of charge."
Puscas said Steaua, currently second in the league, had paid some $920,000 to the FRF.
The FRF said the money had been used to train junior players.
"In the last three years, the FRF took 10 percent from the sums paid to Steaua by UEFA, in earnings from games played in the Champions' league," Puscas added.
Universitatea Craiova also said they want the federation to return money levied from the transfers.

"The total amount of money paid to our club for our players' transfer to Spain, Holland, Israel, Greece or Cyprus was about $5.0 million," Craiova vice-president Marcel Popescu said. "The FRF should return the cut of $500,000 it took."
Some eight first division clubs plan to appeal to the Professional Soccer Clubs League to sort out the issue with the FRF.
